## About this example

This page is a regular Quarto document with executable Python cells. Download
[`quarto-report.qmd`](https://github.com/jeroenjanssens/polars-umap/blob/main/gallery/quarto-report.qmd)
and render it with:

```bash
uv run --with polars-umap --with scikit-learn --with altair --with jupyter \
  quarto render quarto-report.qmd
```
:::

## Introduction

How do posts from different discussion groups relate to each other? This report embeds
posts from three newsgroups as vectors, projects them to 2D with
[polars-umap](https://polars-umap.jeroenjanssens.com), and looks at the structure that
emerges. The newsgroups are about hockey, space and religion.

## Data

```{python}
#| label: setup
import altair as alt
import numpy as np
import polars as pl
from sklearn.datasets import fetch_20newsgroups
from sklearn.decomposition import TruncatedSVD
from sklearn.feature_extraction.text import TfidfVectorizer

import polars_umap as pu

pl.Config(fmt_str_lengths=120, tbl_hide_dataframe_shape=True)

TOPICS = {
    "rec.sport.hockey": "Hockey",
    "sci.space": "Space",
    "talk.religion.misc": "Religion",
}
COLORS = ["#2a78d6", "#eb6834", "#1baf7a"]

news = fetch_20newsgroups(
    subset="all", categories=list(TOPICS), remove=("headers", "footers", "quotes")
)
```

We use the [20 Newsgroups](http://qwone.com/~jason/20Newsgroups/) dataset, with headers,
signatures and quoted replies removed. Each post becomes a 100-dimensional vector: TF-IDF
weights, reduced with a truncated SVD. Any embedding model works the same way from here on.

```{python}
#| label: embed
tfidf = TfidfVectorizer(min_df=3, stop_words="english").fit_transform(news.data)
vectors = TruncatedSVD(n_components=100, random_state=0).fit_transform(tfidf)

posts = pl.DataFrame(
    {
        "text": news.data,
        "topic": [TOPICS[news.target_names[i]] for i in news.target],
        "embedding": vectors.astype(np.float32),
    }
).with_columns(
    # Empty posts have an all-zero vector, for which cosine distance is undefined.
    pl.when(pl.Series(np.linalg.norm(vectors, axis=1) > 0)).then(pl.col("embedding")),
    snippet=pl.col("text").str.replace_all(r"\s+", " ").str.strip_chars().str.slice(0, 120),
)
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-posts
#| tbl-cap: Posts per newsgroup.
posts.group_by("topic").agg(
    posts=pl.len(), empty=pl.col("embedding").is_null().sum()
).sort("topic")
```

## A map of the posts

polars-umap projects the vectors to 2D. Cosine distance suits text vectors, whose length
mostly reflects the length of the post. `null_policy="ignore"` skips the empty posts.

```{python}
#| label: umap
posts = posts.umap.fit_transform(
    "embedding", metric="cosine", null_policy="ignore", random_state=0
)
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-map
#| fig-cap: >-
#|   Newsgroup posts embedded with polars-umap. Hover over a point to read the
#|   start of the post.
(
    alt.Chart(posts.drop_nulls("umap_0").select("topic", "snippet", "umap_0", "umap_1"))
    .mark_circle(size=14, opacity=0.6)
    .encode(
        x=alt.X("umap_0", axis=None),
        y=alt.Y("umap_1", axis=None),
        color=alt.Color(
            "topic:N",
            scale=alt.Scale(domain=list(TOPICS.values()), range=COLORS),
            legend=alt.Legend(title=None, orient="top-left"),
        ),
        tooltip=[alt.Tooltip("topic:N", title="Newsgroup"), alt.Tooltip("snippet:N", title="Post")],
    )
    .properties(width="container", height=480)
    .configure_view(stroke=None)
)
```

@fig-map shows that hockey and space each form a large region of their own. Religion is
more spread out and overlaps with space where posts discuss, for example, cosmology and
creation. The small, dense islands at the edges are near-duplicates: repeated
announcements and very short posts.

## How well are the topics separated?

A simple way to quantify the map: for each post, how many of its 10 nearest neighbors in
the embedding come from the same newsgroup? polars-umap's `knn()` works on the 2D
embedding as well.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-purity
#| tbl-cap: Share of each post's 10 nearest neighbors on the map that come from the same newsgroup.
mapped = posts.drop_nulls("umap_0").with_row_index("row")
neighbors = mapped.select(
    "row", "topic", nn=pu.knn("umap_0", "umap_1", k=11, random_state=0)
).with_columns(nn=pl.col("nn").struct.field("indices").arr.to_list())

(
    neighbors.explode("nn")
    .filter(pl.col("nn") != pl.col("row"))
    .join(mapped.select(nn="row", nn_topic="topic"), on="nn")
    .group_by("topic")
    .agg(same_newsgroup=(pl.col("topic") == pl.col("nn_topic")).mean())
    .sort("topic")
    .with_columns(pl.col("same_newsgroup").round(3))
)
```

## Similar posts

Nearest neighbors in the original 100-dimensional space find posts about the same thing.
Here are the closest posts to one about the Hubble Space Telescope:

```{python}
#| label: tbl-similar
#| tbl-cap: The five posts most similar to a post about the Hubble Space Telescope.
query = (
    posts.with_row_index("row")
    .filter(pl.col("text").str.contains("Hubble") & pl.col("embedding").is_not_null())
    .row(0, named=True)["row"]
)
nn = posts.select(nn=pu.knn("embedding", k=6, metric="cosine", null_policy="ignore", random_state=0))
similar = nn.row(query)[0]
pl.DataFrame({"row": similar["indices"], "distance": similar["distances"]}).join(
    posts.with_row_index("row").select("row", "topic", "snippet"), on="row"
).sort("distance").select("distance", "topic", "snippet").with_columns(pl.col("distance").round(3))
```

The first row is the post itself, at distance 0.

## Conclusion

A few lines of Polars turn raw text vectors into an interpretable map. The newsgroups about
hockey and space form clear clusters. Religion is the most diverse, which matches its "misc"
name. The same pipeline works for any embedding column, and with `.over()` it would produce one
map per group just as easily.
